newsitem.title: UK: Norwich Union to offer 1.3 bln free shares.
newsitem.headline: Norwich Union to offer 1.3 bln free shares.

text.p: British insurance group Norwich Union said on Tuesday that it expected to allocate 1.3 billion free shares to about 2.9 million qualifying members as part of its plan to float on the London Stock Exchange.
The group said it expected its shares to commence trading from June 16.
with-profit members will receive a variable allocation of free shares, subject to a minimum of 300, while non-profit members will receive a fixed allocation of 150 free shares.

Norwich said members could also apply to buy shares, but they had to go for a minimum amount of stock worth 400 pounds and would be allowed a maximum of 100,000 pounds. A non-member could make a minimum application of 1,000 pounds.
The group said it intended to raise another 1.75 billion pounds ($2.8 billion) through an offer of additional shares to members, institutions and other investors.
Out of this amount 1.5 billion pounds will be paid into the with-profit fund of Norwich Union's main life company.
